name: Kelpline Logistics HarbourSkate MX-40 Magnetic Levitation Cargo Sled
product_name: Kelpline Logistics HarbourSkate MX-40 Magnetic Levitation Cargo Sled
description:
The HarbourSkate MX-40 is a fully autonomous, track-bound magnetic levitation cargo sled designed to operate within Meridian 88's submerged and semi-flooded lower-tier dock infrastructure. Each unit rides a passive ferromagnetic rail embedded in waterproofed concrete channels, using onboard superconducting coils chilled by a closed-loop cryogenic nitrogen circuit to achieve frictionless glide at speeds up to 180 km/h in enclosed corridors. Payload capacity tops out at 4,200 kilograms per sled unit, and sleds can be chain-linked in automated convoy configurations of up to twelve units managed by a single Cinderblock AI routing node. The MX-40 distinguishes itself from competing cargo systems through its amphibious transition capability: when rail segments are flooded, the sled's hull shifts to a sealed buoyancy mode, activating a rear-mounted impeller to maintain cargo movement through partially submerged sections without requiring infrastructure shutdown or rerouting.

The system was developed in response to the chronic flooding of Meridian 88's Port Sublevel districts, where traditional wheeled logistics broke down entirely during seasonal Great Lakes surge events. Kelpline integrated pressure-adaptive hull plating sourced from Palladian Construction composites and a redundant navigation stack from Cinderblock AI that allows the sled to make real-time rerouting decisions when sensors detect rail submersion depth exceeding safe maglev thresholds. Each sled broadcasts its status on the Saltmarsh Telecom AtmoMesh frequencies, feeding logistics data back to Kelpline's central dispatch.

The MX-40 fleet is leased primarily to Tier 2 and Tier 3 licensed freight operators who cannot afford the aerial drone corridors maintained by higher-tier logistics providers. The sleds have become so embedded in lower-city supply chains that entire black-market economies have grown around hijacking or temporarily rerouting sled convoys, a practice known colloquially as 'rail ghosting.'

social_impact: The HarbourSkate MX-40 has quietly restructured economic survival in Meridian 88's flood-prone lower districts by making consistent supply delivery possible where wheeled transport failed seasonally. Tier 4 communities that once faced weeks-long supply disruptions during surge events now receive continuous logistics throughput — but Kelpline's lease model means any operator who misses payments loses sled access instantly, creating a new class of infrastructure debt bondage. Sled corridor access has become a political currency, with district bosses negotiating routing rights as leverage over food and medicine supply.
story_hooks: A Kelpline sled convoy carrying emergency medical supplies has been 'rail ghosted' and rerouted into a sealed flood district — someone inside the company sold the override codes
A player character discovers that a specific MX-40 unit has been making unauthorized stops in a section of the rail network that doesn't exist on any official map
Cinderblock AI's routing node for the MX-40 fleet begins making statistically inexplicable decisions that seem to favor one freight operator — is it corruption, emergent behavior, or something else?
A Tier 4 community has jury-rigged three decommissioned MX-40 sleds into a mobile living platform navigating the flooded sublevel tunnels — Kelpline wants them back
